# [Baseline] - WIN - D - Cloud PC Session Security

Secures the session on a Windows 365 Cloud PC or Azure Virtual Desktop session host: nothing copied from the virtual desktop to the local device, no COM, LPT or USB devices redirected, the session disconnected on lock, screen capture from the local device blocked and a watermark with the connection ID across the desktop.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | OpenIntuneBaseline Windows 365 v1.0 — Device Security - D - Connectivity Settings and Resource Redirection, without the four settings that [Baseline] - WIN - D - Remote Desktop and RPC already sets; IntuneAdmin — Baseline - AVD - Enable screen capture protection and Enable watermarking |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Cloud_PC_Session_Security.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Cloud_PC_Session_Security.json) |

> Complements what [Baseline] - WIN - D - Remote Desktop and RPC already sets on every device (password prompt on connect, secure RPC, encryption level High, no drive redirection); those four are deliberately not repeated here. Clipboard from server to client is off (OIB); from client to server it stays allowed. Screen capture protection on 'client' and not on 'client and server' as in IntuneAdmin: data already stays in the virtual desktop that way, and the Snipping Tool inside the session keeps working for a service desk report. Consequence: anyone sharing the desktop in a Teams meeting from the local device sees black — share from Teams inside the session. Windows App on iOS and Android only connects if an app protection policy on Windows App blocks screen capture (see IOS/AppConfiguration and AND/AppConfiguration). The watermark works on a full desktop, not on RemoteApp. BitLocker does not belong on a Cloud PC: exclude SEC-Cloud-PC from [Baseline] - WIN - D - BitLocker and [Baseline] - WIN - U - Compliance BitLocker, or assign those with a filter on deviceModel.
